spoilerRisks.field: Entity summaries, aliases, roles, memberships, locations, related, owners, users
spoilerRisks.issue: These are cumulative final-scope snapshots. Entity appearance in an earlier book does not authorize showing its final fields at an earlier spoiler boundary. Gate the whole snapshot by latest book or use explicit fact-level reveal metadata.
Many inferred memberships have from=-10000 and a broad books list. These are graph lifetimes or generated defaults, not reliable first-reveal metadata. Do not use from as a spoiler reveal timestamp.
Arc summaries repeat the end of a multi-chapter arc in earlier chapter entries. Safe at completed-book boundaries; unsafe for precise chapter-progress spoiler protection.
Anchors are broad arc associations, sometimes repeated over many chapters. Show these as related arc anchors unless the exact chapter association has been verified.
Current Coppermind pages contain Wind and Truth and later spoilers. Label external sources as potentially containing spoilers beyond the selected boundary.

chronologyWarnings.issue: All describe the same assassination night, but sort values are -1,100,300,600. sort mixes presentation order with in-world chronology. A single chronological axis must group them in1167 and retain reveal/source order separately.
The event is revealed in ROW chapter117 but occurs after Narak near the ending of WoR. sort832 is reading position, not when it happened.

sort342 places an event tied to OB chapters111–113 among early/middle-book events; research and revelation are conflated. Split research from final discovery, or keep the ordering explicitly approximate.
WoR I-3 occurs before I-9 in reading order, but recovered sort152 places it after145. This may not establish an in-world contradiction, but it shows sort is not a verified reading sequence.
Recovered dateLabel says soon after the Rift. A precise interval is not asserted here; source verification should precede using this as a dated chronological claim.
Ancient sort values are illustrative ordering coordinates, not canonical year values. Display relative labels with uncertainty; do not label these numbers as dates or calculate durations from them.
